questions.question: The monumental public structure known as the 'Great Bath' was excavated at which Harappan site?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath, a large rectangular tank in a courtyard surrounded by a corridor, was situated on the Citadel at Mohenjodaro.

questions.question: Which animal motif is most frequently engraved on standard Harappan steatite stamp seals?
options: B) The one-horned unicorn mythical beast
questions.explanation: The most common animal depicted on Harappan seals is the mythical one-horned animal commonly termed the unicorn.

questions.question: At which Harappan settlement in Gujarat was a massive tidal brick dockyard basin excavated?
questions.explanation: Lothal featured a large brick basin identified by archaeologists as a tidal dockyard connected to the Bhogavo river.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: What was the imperial capital of the Mauryan Empire during the reigns of Chandragupta and Ashoka?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) was the fortified capital city of the vast Mauryan Empire.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Who was the royal grandfather of Ashoka who laid the foundation of the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan dynasty with the strategic guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which ancient script was predominantly used to carve Ashoka's rock and pillar edicts across northern and eastern India?
questions.explanation: Most Ashokan inscriptions across the heartland of the subcontinent were written in Prakrit using the Brahmi script.

questions.question: In which classical language was the epic Mahabharata originally composed?
questions.explanation: The Mahabharata was originally composed in Sanskrit, using simpler syntactic structures than classical court poetry.

questions.question: In the epic Mahabharata, Draupadi's union with the five Pandava brothers represents which marriage custom?
questions.explanation: Draupadi was married simultaneously to all five Pandava brothers, exemplifying polyandrous marital union.

questions.question: According to the Purusha Sukta and orthodox Dharmashastras, which varna occupied the highest rank in society?
questions.explanation: The Brahmanical varna order placed Brahmanas at the top of the cosmic hierarchy as teachers and performers of sacrifices.

questions.question: Vardhamana Mahavira is revered in Jain religious tradition as which Tirthankara in succession?
questions.explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and final Tirthankara of the present cosmic age, preceded by Parshvanatha.

questions.question: At which sacred town did Gautama Buddha attain his final demise and Mahaparinirvana?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha entered Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar in modern Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The Great Stupa that remained intact through the centuries and stands well-preserved in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh is:
questions.explanation: The Sanchi Stupa survived nearly intact and was protected by the Begums of Bhopal and the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.question: The 14th-century traveler Ibn Battuta set out on his global travels from which city and country in North Africa?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, into an educated family of Islamic legal scholars (qazis).

questions.question: Francois Bernier, who lived at the Mughal court for twelve years, was a native of which European nation?
questions.explanation: Francois Bernier was a French physician, philosopher, and traveler who visited India between 1656 and 1668.

questions.question: Al-Biruni arrived in northern India in the 11th century accompanied by the army of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni was brought to Ghazni from Khwarizm by Sultan Mahmud and accompanied his expeditions into Punjab.

questions.question: The 16th-century poet-saint Mirabai composed emotional devotional songs (bhajans) dedicated to which incarnation of God?
questions.explanation: Mirabai regarded Lord Krishna (Giridhar Gopal) as her eternal divine consort and beloved.

questions.question: The world-famous Sufi dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti is located in which historic city of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti established his hospice at Ajmer, which became a great pilgrimage destination visited even by Akbar.

questions.question: Guru Nanak Dev, the revered founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469 at which village in Punjab?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak was born at Nankana Sahib (formerly Rai Bhoi di Talwandi) near the river Ravi.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra by which two brothers?
options: A) Krishnadeva Raya and Achyuta Raya
B) Saluva Narasimha and Vira Narasimha
questions.explanation: The brothers Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which manifestation of Shiva served as the guardian royal deity of the Vijayanagara kings at Hampi?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara kings claimed to rule on behalf of the god Virupaksha, signing official orders as 'Sri Virupaksha'.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Which volume of Abu'l Fazl's official chronicle 'Akbarnama' is titled the 'Ain-i-Akbari'?
questions.explanation: The Akbarnama comprises three volumes, the third and most famous being the Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor abolished the discriminatory pilgrim tax in 1563 and the jizya tax in 1564?
questions.explanation: Akbar demonstrated his policy of Sulh-i Kul by abolishing both the pilgrim tax and jizya on non-Muslim subjects.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In Persian administrative chronicles of the Mughal Empire, peasants and cultivators were designated by which term?
questions.explanation: Mughal records used raiyat (plural riaya) or asami to refer to ordinary peasant cultivators.

questions.question: In which British Indian province was the Permanent Settlement of land revenue first promulgated in 1793?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and Bihar in 1793.

questions.question: Which indigenous hill-dwelling community of the Rajmahal region practiced shifting cultivation using the hoe?
questions.explanation: The Paharias lived in the Rajmahal hills and practiced shifting cultivation with the hoe (kural).

questions.question: Which sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857?
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey mutinied at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857, protesting against the greased cartridges.

questions.question: Which heroic queen led the revolt of 1857 from the central Indian fortress of Jhansi against British forces?
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai led the revolt in Jhansi after Lord Dalhousie annexed the state under the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.question: In which country did Mahatma Gandhi first forge and experiment with his technique of non-violent Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi developed the philosophy and practice of Satyagraha during his stay in South Africa from 1893 to 1914.

questions.question: The tragic massacre of unarmed citizens at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919 took place in which city?
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on an unarmed crowd assembled at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was officially adopted, enacted, and signed by the Constituent Assembly on:
questions.explanation: The Constitution was finalized and adopted on 26 November 1949, and came into full legal effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: Which distant Harappan commercial outpost in northeastern Afghanistan was established specifically to procure precious blue lapis lazuli?
questions.explanation: Shortughai was founded near the Badakhshan mines in Afghanistan as an outpost for sourcing deep-blue lapis lazuli.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Before shifting the capital to Pataliputra in the 4th century BCE, what was the initial fortified capital of the Magadha kingdom?
questions.explanation: Rajagriha ('House of the King'), surrounded by five natural hills, was the earliest fortified capital of Magadha.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which special administrative officers were appointed by Emperor Ashoka to preach and disseminate the principles of Dhamma?
questions.explanation: Ashoka created the new cadre of Dhamma Mahamattas to tour the provinces and propagate moral conduct and mutual respect.

questions.question: In early Sanskrit literature, the kinship term 'Kula' was specifically used to designate:
options: A) The entire regional caste guild
B) Families or domestic kinship units
D) An alliance of frontier nomadic tribes
questions.explanation: Sanskrit texts use kula to designate families, jnati for larger kin networks, and vamsha for lineage descent.

questions.question: Among the five major ethical vows (Mahavratas) observed by Jain ascetics, which vow requires complete non-possession of worldly property?
questions.explanation: The five Jain vows are Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truthfulness), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), and Aparigraha (non-possession).

questions.question: In his travelogue, Ibn Battuta expressed great fascination with two botanical products unfamiliar to his homeland: which were they?
options: A) Tea leaves and rubber trees
C) Coffee cherries and nutmeg seeds
D) The betel leaf (paan) and the coconut palm
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta dedicated vivid sections describing the coconut palm (likening its nut to a human face) and the betel vine.

questions.question: Followers of the Lingayat (Virashaiva) tradition in Karnataka are distinguished by which physical sacred emblem?
options: A) A miniature stone linga enclosed in a silver casket worn looped around the neck
B) A consecrated iron dagger sheathed at the waist
C) A sacred wooden rosary of 108 sandalwood beads
D) A saffron turban inscribed with Vedic hymns
questions.explanation: Lingayats are literally 'wearers of the linga' and carry a small Shiva linga in a pendant worn over the left shoulder.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The monumental, towering gateway structures erected at the entrances of South Indian temples by Vijayanagara rulers were known as:
questions.explanation: Raya Gopurams were massive royal entrance gateways designed to signal imperial patronage from miles away.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In Mughal village self-governance, the council of village elders was headed by a chief known as the:
questions.explanation: The village headman was called Muqaddam or Mandal, chosen with the consensus of village elders and confirmed by the zamindar.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Which plant originating in the Americas arrived in northern India via the Deccan during the closing years of Akbar's reign?
questions.explanation: Tobacco arrived in the Deccan around 1600; Akbar was presented with a tobacco pipe by Asad Beg, and Jahangir later banned its consumption.

questions.question: Under the terms of the Bengal Permanent Settlement (1793), what proportion of the collected revenue was the zamindar required to hand over to the Company?
questions.explanation: The East India Company retained 10/11ths of the collected rental demand, leaving 1/11th to the zamindar.

questions.question: In Delhi, while Bahadur Shah Zafar was the nominal figurehead, actual military leadership of the rebel sepoys was led by:
options: B) Subedar Bakht Khan of Bareilly
questions.explanation: Subedar Bakht Khan arrived from Bareilly with a contingent of rebel troops and assumed supreme military command in Delhi.

questions.question: In February 1916, Mahatma Gandhi delivered his first major public address in India on the occasion of the opening of which institution?
options: D) Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics
questions.explanation: Gandhi addressed the opening of BHU in February 1916, admonishing the privileged elite for their indifference to the poor peasants.

questions.question: Which woman member of the Constituent Assembly from Madras passionately argued that the Constitution must abolish all legal discriminations against women?
questions.explanation: Ammu Swaminathan declared that the Constitution had given equal rights to all citizens, fulfilling Indian women's aspirations.

questions.question: What was the total numerical membership originally envisioned for the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan originally fixed 389 members, which was reduced to 299 following the partition of India.

questions.question: The architectural layout of the Great Granary excavated at Harappa consisted of:
options: A) A circular subterranean brick silo surrounded by four concentric fortification moats
B) Twelve rectangular storage blocks arranged symmetrically in two parallel rows of six units separated by a central corridor
C) A single colossal stone chamber resting on forty monolithic limestone columns
D) Eight underground vaults interconnected by lead drainage pipes
questions.explanation: The granary at Harappa comprised 12 independent blocks arranged in two rows of six, raised on sleeper walls with air ducts.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In the anonymous 1st-century CE Greek navigational guide 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea', what was the Hellenized name assigned to the port of Bharuch?
questions.explanation: The Periplus describes Barygaza (Bharuch in Gujarat) as a vital western emporium exporting cotton textiles, agate, and silk.

questions.question: In the spiritual genealogy of the Chishti silsila, who was the direct spiritual master (Pir) of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya?
options: D) Shaikh Fariduddin Ganj-i Shakar (Baba Farid)
questions.explanation: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya received his spiritual initiation and succession from Baba Farid of Ajodhan.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: The Dahsala land revenue assessment system finalized under Akbar's finance minister Raja Todar Mal was characterized by:
options: A) Levying a fixed annual tribute in gold bullion regardless of whether the land was farmed
B) Calculating the state revenue share based on the average agricultural yield and market prices of various crops over the preceding ten years
C) Auctioning village assessment rights to European joint-stock chartered companies
D) Confiscating one-third of all standing crops at the time of each autumn harvest
questions.explanation: The Ain-i-Dahsala instituted by Todar Mal in 1580 calculated average crop production and prices over the previous decade (1570-1580).

questions.question: During the Constituent Assembly debates on federal distribution of finances, which member warned that an overly centralized Centre would make provinces dependent and crumble like an 'inverted pyramid'?
questions.explanation: K. Santhanam argued that fiscal centralisation would burden the Centre and leave provinces starved of developmental funds.
